newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian portfolio rules apply to gvt securities.
newsitem.headline: Romanian portfolio rules apply to gvt securities.

text.p: Romania's new portfolio investment rules, setting tax on capital gains repatriation at four percent, apply equally to government securities, according to a draft published on Friday in the daily newspaper Adevarul.
To become effective the decree, adopted this week by the new centrist coalition government, must still be published in the Official Gazette.

The long-awaited portfolio rules, demanded by Western lenders and investors, won wide praise and are seen as pivotal for capital market development, sluggish in the seven years since Romania ended communist rule.

If capital gains withdrawn sooner than a year exceed 25 percent of the total value of the investment, authorities will impose an extra tax of 0.1 percent per day of the amount repatriated calculated for the whole year, a government statement said on Wednesday.
Under the new rules, capital gains may be repatriated only in the currency in which the initial investment was made. The invested capital is not subject to taxation if repatriated.
But the new rules make no specific reference to the access of foreigners to the securities market.
Romania has so far funded the bulk of its budget deficits through issues of treasury bills, most on short-term.
A secondary market for government papers was nearly non-existent in the absence of proper framework for primary and secondary trading, adopted only two months ago.
The market has since become more active with high-returning yields and the newly-stable leu currency has prompted growing foreign interest in the finance ministry's papers.

The total of outstanding domestic bills is estimated at about 4.2 trillion lei. Romania's internal public debt was 6.69 trillion lei at end-1996. ($7,162 lei) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
